evidence.text: - Call withdraw or redeem specifying victim as owner and attacker as receiver
These functions should verify that msg.sender has permission to act on behalf of owner. However, they only call:
The spendSelfAllowance function checks only that allowance(owner, owner) >= shares. It never checks that msg.sender has any relationship to owner or permission to burn their shares.
The root cause is that ERC4626 vaults include this check:

This validates that either the caller IS the owner, or the caller has an allowance FROM the owner. The WERC7575Vault completely omits this validation, relying only on the self-allowance check which is irrelevant to the caller's authorization.

links.reported_relation: The vault relies only on the self-allowance check and omits the caller-is-owner-or-has-allowance validation, so a non-owner caller can burn the owner's shares.
The attacker calls withdraw with victim as owner and attacker as receiver, causing the victim's shares to be burned while the attacker receives the assets.
